claims: NASA launched the Artemis II mission on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the moon since 1972.
Artemis II launched from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Artemis II is the first mission to test the Orion spacecraft's life support systems with astronauts.
The launch time of Artemis II is 6:35 p.m. ET (2235 GMT).
The crew of Artemis II is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The mission goal of Artemis II is a 10-day flight around the moon to test systems for future lunar landings.
The Artemis II mission utilizes the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the Orion spacecraft.
If delayed, subsequent launch opportunities for Artemis II were available starting April 2, 2026.
The Artemis II mission verifies that all of Orion's systems, including the crew module, operate as designed in deep space with astronauts aboard.
